descriptions.breast_benign: Benign breast tissue displays preserved glandular architecture characterized by well-formed ducts and terminal duct lobular units with a distinct dual layer of inner cuboidal epithelial and outer attenuated myoepithelial cells. Nuclei are uniformly small, monomorphic, and round-to-oval with smooth nuclear membranes, finely dispersed bland chromatin, and an absence of hyperchromasia or marked pleomorphism. The surrounding background features dense, eosinophilic fibrillar collagenous or pale myxoid stroma sharply contrasting with the orderly, basophilic epithelial aggregates and patent glandular lumina.
descriptions.breast_malignant: Infiltrating cohesive nests, irregular cords, poorly formed tubules, or single-file arrays of atypical epithelial cells permeate a pale-eosinophilic, desmoplastic, and collagenous stroma. Neoplastic cells exhibit high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios, marked pleomorphism, and enlarged hyperchromatic nuclei characterized by irregular contours, coarse or clumped chromatin texture, and prominent macronucleoli. Deeply basophilic nuclear staining with frequent atypical mitotic figures contrasts sharply with the variable eosinophilic to amphophilic cytoplasm and the surrounding fibrous extracellular matrix.
descriptions.colon_aca: Infiltrative, irregularly branching, back-to-back, or cribriform glandular structures disrupt the normal architecture, frequently containing central luminal necrotic debris and invading a pale eosinophilic, desmoplastic stroma. The neoplastic epithelial cells are pseudostratified, pleomorphic columnar to cuboidal, featuring enlarged, hyperchromatic, elongated to vesicular nuclei with loss of normal polarity, coarse chromatin texture, and prominent nucleoli. Histopathology sections exhibit a strong staining contrast between intensely basophilic nuclear clusters, moderate amphophilic-to-eosinophilic cytoplasm, and areas of pale basophilic extracellular mucin with frequent atypical mitotic figures.
descriptions.colon_n: Normal colonic mucosa is characterized by parallel, evenly spaced, test-tube-like crypts of Lieberkühn oriented perpendicularly in the lamina propria without architectural distortion. The epithelium is composed of simple columnar enterocytes interspersed with abundant round, clear-to-pale mucin-filled goblet cells exhibiting small, monomorphic, basally located oval nuclei with smooth contours and fine chromatin. On H&E staining, the apical cytoplasmic mucin appears transparent or faintly basophilic, contrasting distinctly with the deep blue-purple polarized basal nuclei and the moderately cellular, eosinophilic fibromuscular stroma.
descriptions.lung_aca: Malignant epithelial proliferation arranged in irregular glandular, acinar, papillary, or solid nested architectures infiltrating an eosinophilic desmoplastic stroma. The tumor cells exhibit pleomorphic cuboidal-to-columnar morphology with enlarged, hyperchromatic or vesicular nuclei, coarse chromatin, and prominent macronucleoli. Cytoplasm is moderate to abundant with eosinophilic to amphophilic staining, frequently displaying intracytoplasmic mucin vacuoles or luminal pale-basophilic mucinous secretions.
descriptions.lung_n: Normal lung parenchyma exhibits an open, delicate lace-like architecture dominated by large, optically clear alveolar airspaces bounded by ultra-thin alveolar septa. The septal walls contain flattened, elongated nuclei of type I pneumocytes and capillary endothelial cells, interspersed with occasional small, rounded cuboidal type II pneumocytes. H&E staining demonstrates thin, light-pink eosinophilic collagenous septa punctuated by sparse, small basophilic nuclei, set against a predominant white luminal background occasionally containing isolated alveolar macrophages.
descriptions.lung_scc: Neoplastic cells are organized into cohesive solid sheets, anastomosing cords, and infiltrative nests with prominent intercellular bridges and characteristic concentric keratin pearls. The individual cells are large and polygonal, displaying dense, glassy, intensely eosinophilic cytoplasm with sharply defined cell borders. Nuclei are markedly pleomorphic, hyperchromatic, and angulated with coarse chromatin, prominent nucleoli, and frequent atypical mitoses against a desmoplastic or necrotic background.
descriptions.oral_normal_oral_cavity: Normal oral mucosa displays a well-organized, stratified squamous epithelium characterized by orderly maturation from small, cuboidal basal cells with oval hyperchromatic nuclei up to expanded polygonal spinous cells and flattened superficial squames. The overlying epithelium exhibits a gradient from basophilic basal layers to abundant, glassy eosinophilic cytoplasm toward the surface, separated by delicate intercellular bridges. Beneath a sharp, undulating basement membrane, the lamina propria contains loose to dense eosinophilic fibrillar collagen, scattered spindle-shaped fibroblasts, delicate capillaries, and occasional underlying lobules of pale-staining minor salivary glands or skeletal muscle bundles without atypia.
descriptions.oral_oscc: Infiltrative nests, irregular cords, and cohesive sheets of malignant squamous epithelial cells invade the subepithelial stroma, often eliciting a marked desmoplastic and inflammatory stromal response. Neoplastic cells are large and polygonal with distinct intercellular bridges, abundant dense eosinophilic cytoplasm, and enlarged pleomorphic nuclei featuring coarse chromatin, prominent nucleoli, and atypical mitotic figures. Distinctive diagnostic hallmarks include concentric, brightly eosinophilic keratin pearls and individual cell dyskeratosis contrasted against hyperchromatic, deeply basophilic nuclear clusters.
descriptions.ovarian_clear_cell: Neoplastic proliferation exhibits tubulocystic, papillary, or solid architectural arrangements often set within dense, hyalinized eosinophilic stroma. The tumor cells are polygonal or distinctively hobnail-shaped, featuring voluminous optically clear, glycogen-rich cytoplasm with sharply defined cell membranes, alongside variants with granular eosinophilic cytoplasm. Nuclei are markedly enlarged, hyperchromatic, and pleomorphic with conspicuous macronucleoli, characteristically bulging into cystic and tubular lumina.
descriptions.ovarian_endometri: Tissue sections demonstrate crowded, back-to-back tubular and cribriform glandular architecture mimicking proliferative endometrium, frequently accompanied by distinct eosinophilic squamous morules within a desmoplastic or altered stroma. The neoplastic epithelium consists of pseudostratified tall columnar cells with uniform apical borders, amphophilic-to-eosinophilic cytoplasm, and oval-to-elongated hyperchromatic nuclei exhibiting coarse chromatin and variable nucleoli. The glands form well-defined, smooth lumina often containing intraluminal necrotic debris or mucin, distinctly contrasting with the surrounding basophilic glandular lining and dense stromal background.
descriptions.ovarian_mucinous: Ovarian mucinous neoplasms typically present with cystic, glandular, or complex confluent architectures lined by single or stratified layers of tall columnar epithelium. The individual tumor cells exhibit abundant pale, foamy-to-clear apical cytoplasm distended by mucin droplets, compressing uniform to moderately atypical oval nuclei toward the basal membrane. On standard H&E staining, luminal spaces are filled with distinctive smooth to wispy, pale basophilic-to-amphophilic extracellular mucin that sharply contrasts with the dark, hyperchromatic basal nuclei.
descriptions.ovarian_non_cancerous: Non-cancerous ovarian parenchyma demonstrates an orderly architecture composed of dense, cellular stroma with spindle-shaped fibroblastic cells arranged in whorled or intersecting fascicles, often accompanied by benign surface epithelium, inclusion cysts, or follicles with uniform granulosa cell layers. The stromal and epithelial cells possess bland, oval to elongated nuclei with smooth contours, fine powdery chromatin, inconspicuous nucleoli, and a complete lack of significant cytologic pleomorphism or atypical mitotic activity. Hematoxylin and eosin staining highlights a fibrillar eosinophilic collagenous extracellular matrix surrounding evenly distributed, normochromatic basophilic nuclei without areas of destructive infiltration, marked architectural complexity, or tumor necrosis.
descriptions.ovarian_serous: The tissue exhibits complex architectural patterns including branching papillary fronds, micropapillary clusters, and slit-like glandular or solid arrangements supported by a desmoplastic stroma. Individual tumor cells are cuboidal to columnar with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios, featuring markedly enlarged, hyperchromatic, pleomorphic nuclei with coarse chromatin and prominent eosinophilic nucleoli. The cytoplasm is moderately amphophilic to eosinophilic, frequently accompanied by brisk atypical mitotic figures and distinct, deeply basophilic, concentrically laminated psammoma bodies.

prompt_template: You are a pathologist writing a detailed morphological description for the class {class_name!r} (dataset: {dataset}), to be encoded by a vision-language model's text tower and compared against histopathology image patches. Cover: cell/nuclear shape, arrangement or architecture, texture, and any distinctive staining pattern. 2-4 sentences. Output only the description, no preamble, no quotes.
